findings.title: Credential saved as the SafeParseReturn wrapper instead of the token data
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result object ({success, data}), not the parsed token. Before this change `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the token itself. Now `key` is the wrapper, so prisma writes {success:true,data:{...}} into the credential. On the next load, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) fails and Google Calendar breaks for every user whose token was refreshed.

findings.title: prisma used without import; refresh runs on every instantiation
findings.body: `prisma` is never imported in this file, so the new prisma.credential.update call throws a ReferenceError (or fails type-check). In addition, the refresh request is sent on every service construction, the refreshed access token is never passed to the jsforce Connection (it still uses the old credentialKey.access_token), and the sync endpoint path (refreshOAuthTokens) is not used at all.

findings.title: credentialId passed where userId is expected
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens takes a userId as its third argument, but this call passes credentialId. When sync is enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for tokens for the wrong Cal.com user, which can hand out another user's credentials.

findings.title: Sync path returns a fetch Response, which callers do not expect
findings.body: When sync is enabled this function returns a raw fetch Response. Several callers expect a different shape: Google reads `res.data`, Zoho and Bigin read `tokenInfo.data`, and HubSpot uses the result directly as a token object. All of these break when sync is enabled. The request also sends no auth header or secret to the sync endpoint.

findings.title: Bogus zod schema keys
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]". Both computed keys collapse to that same key, and the first one requires a number, so validation of real token responses fails. Separately, the function injects the fake refresh_token "refresh_token" when none is returned, and that value is then persisted; Zoom and Webex would store it and use it for later refreshes.

findings.title: Non-constant-time secret comparison; no method check
findings.body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information. The handler accepts any HTTP method. Invalid input causes zod parse and JSON/decrypt errors to throw as 500s. Use timingSafeEqual, restrict to POST, and return 400 on invalid input.

findings.title: Wrong app slug 'zoomvideo'
findings.body: The Zoom app slug is "zoom", not "zoomvideo". The sync endpoint will receive a slug that does not match what the webhook handler and the app store use, so the parent application cannot resolve the right app.
